name: Container freight
summary: Drewry container index fell 3% to $4,176 per 40ft on 19 Nov, a fourth weekly fall but still above the $4,000 Alert line
state: Drewry's World Container Index fell 3% to $4,176 per 40ft container on 19 Nov, its fourth consecutive weekly decline but 126% higher than a year earlier and above the $4,000 Alert line (Drewry). Shanghai–New York fell 9% to $8,194 and Shanghai–Los Angeles 5% to $7,026, while Shanghai–Genoa rose 6% to $4,436 and Shanghai–Rotterdam was flat at $3,496. Drewry expects transpacific rates to fall further and Asia–Europe rates to rise on December surcharges.
for_you: Higher shipping costs tend to feed into the price and availability of imported goods, especially from Asia. Importers and retailers are most exposed; consumer effects usually lag by several weeks.
basis_detail: Drewry World Container Index / Freightos Baltic Index
basis_by: Drewry World Container Index / Freightos Baltic Index
why: Container rates feed through to goods prices months later; spikes are an early inflation and supply-chain warning.
drivers: Chokepoint diversions, capacity, demand, port congestion, tariffs front-running.

rubric.normal: Drewry World Container Index < $2,500/FEU and 1-month change < +30%.
